title: Japan Ke 3 Paise Wale Tarike
note:
METHOD THREE — KAKEIBO. Fourteen scenes and the chapter's longest quiet
     stretch, so the variance is carried by the ground and by three drawn
     mechanisms rather than by layout churn.

     Ground arc: warm on the book itself -> amber on 1904 -> neutral through
     the shelf and the blank page -> green on the method -> cool on why it was
     new -> red on the four categories that came later and its held crop ->
     neutral through what survives -> green on the four and their order ->
     neutral on paper and the app -> amber out on 7.1%.

     Archetypes: A A D A D A A A A B A A D B. s65/s66 are a matched-frame hold
     (one photograph, a crop change across the boundary) so they keep one
     archetype and one continued push, per the shipped cut's own ken direction.

     Three drawn layers: a hundred and twenty-one annual volumes with FOUR
     MISSING (a shelf photograph shows many spines; it cannot show an absence),
     the year cut into twelve with the saving coming off the top of each, and
     an app pointing backwards against a ledger pointing forwards. Everything
     else is art-off — a drawn ledger over a photographed ledger, a drawn tick
     over a photographed underline, four drawn boxes over four photographed
     lines are all the depictive failure.

s59.comment:
6.1 · A · PLATE · no role · warm — KAKEIBO. A hand-ruled ledger with a pen
     on it; the object is the subject.

s60.comment:
6.2 · A · PLATE · target · amber — 1904, Hani Motoko. A Meiji book cover
     under a dated claim.

s61.comment:
6.3 · D · BAND · no role · neutral — STILL PRINTED. A shelf of identical
     spines can show MANY; it cannot show FOUR MISSING. One volume per year from
     1904, and the wartime gap marked in warn — the only thing on this frame the
     photograph could not have said.

s64.comment:
6.6 · A · PLATE · no role · cool — WHY IT WAS NEW. An inkwell and a nib: the
     decision, before it is made.

s65.comment:
6.7 · A · PLATE · warn · red — THE FOUR CATEGORIES, which came later. The
     photograph is already four separate piles; drawing four boxes on it is the
     rule-8 failure exactly.

s66.comment:
6.8 · A · PLATE · no role · neutral — SAY IT PLAINLY. Matched-frame hold:
     the same photograph as s65 on a tighter crop, and the shipped ken keeps its
     direction across the boundary so the two read as one continuous push.

s67.comment: 6.9 · A · PLATE · no role · neutral — WHAT SURVIVES. A dated diary page.

s68.comment:
6.10 · B · FIGURE · fund · green — THE FOUR. The photograph is four
     handwritten lines, so four drawn lines would be a tracing. What is drawn is
     the ORDER: the second row is lit and the others are not, because the whole
     claim of the next scene is that two comes before three.

     on the frame.
